properties.areaDesc: Sierra Nevada of Sierra-Nevada-Placer Counties Above 5000 ft Including Interstate 80; Sierra Nevada of El Dorado-Amador-Northern Alpine Counties Above 5000 ft Including Highway 50; Sierra Nevada of Calaveras-Tuolumne-Southern Alpine Counties Above 5000 ft
properties.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued October 31 at 11:45AM PDT until November 1 at 7:00AM PST by NWS Sacramento CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Snow expected for elevations above 7000 feet. Total snow
accumulations up to 10 inches, with up to 18 inches at the highest
peaks. Minor accumulations of up to 3 inches possible down to 6000
feet.

* WHERE...Northern Sierra above 7000 feet, including Highway 50 and
Interstate 80.

* WHEN...Until 7 AM PST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Plan on slippery travel conditions and minor travel
delays, with chain controls possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Snow levels 7000 to 8000 feet through this
evening, lowering to 5500 to 6500 feet overnight. Heaviest snowfall
expected tonight into Sunday morning. Light flurries to a dusting
possible down to 5500 feet with measurable accumulations remaining
above 6000 feet.
properties.instruction:
Check the latest road conditions from Caltrans online at
quickmap.dot.ca.gov or dial 5 1 1.

Be prepared for slippery roads. Slow down and use caution while
driving. Be prepared for chain controls and follow any road
restrictions. If you are going outside, watch your first few steps
taken on stairs, sidewalks, and driveways. These surfaces could be
icy and slippery, increasing your risk of a fall and injury.

properties.areaDesc: Lake Havasu and Fort Mohave; Lake Mead - AZ side; Lake Mohave - AZ side; San Bernardino County-Upper Colorado River Valley; Lake Mead - NV side; Lake Mohave - NV side
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 31 at 9:45AM PDT until November 2 at 4:00AM PST by NWS Las Vegas NV
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall will be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of northwest Arizona, including the following
areas, Lake Havasu and Fort Mohave, Lake Mead - AZ side and Lake
Mohave - AZ side, southeast California, including the following
area, San Bernardino County-Upper Colorado River Valley, and
southern Nevada, including the following areas, Lake Mead - NV side
and Lake Mohave - NV side.

* WHEN...From this evening through late Sunday night.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water
crossings may be flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Moderate to heavy rain is possible at times tonight through
Sunday night. Between a half an inch and an inch of rain will be
possible. With saturated soils and significant run off expected,
flash flooding  may occur.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WATCH NOW IN EFFECT FROM THIS EVENING THROUGH LATE SUNDAY NIGHT

properties.areaDesc: Coastal North Bay Including Point Reyes National Seashore; San Francisco Peninsula Coast
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 31 at 4:45AM PDT until October 31 at 6:00PM PDT by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to 1.5 ft of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Pacific Coast.

* WHEN...Until 6 PM PDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 1.5 feet above normal (7.3 ft MLLW) at 03:44
PM on Saturday 10/31. These predictions include up to 1.5 ft of
surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding
threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along
the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay,
respectively.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

respectively.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal Del Norte; Northern Coastal Humboldt; Southwestern Humboldt; Coastal Mendocino
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued October 30 at 10:05PM PDT until November 2 at 10:00PM PST by NWS Eureka CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Increased threat of sneaker waves expected.

* WHERE...Coastal Del Norte, Northern Coastal Humboldt,
Southwestern Humboldt and Coastal Mendocino Counties.

* WHEN...From Sunday evening through Monday evening.

* IMPACTS...Large, unexpected waves can sweep across the beach
without warning, sweeping people into the sea from rocks,
jetties, and beaches. These sneaker waves can also move large
objects such as logs, crushing anyone caught underneath.
properties.instruction:
Don't be fooled by an ocean that looks calm.  There can be
30 minutes of small waves before a sneaker wave strikes.  Avoid
rocks and jetties. Avoid steep beaches.  Stay much farther back
from the water and never turn your back on the ocean.
